run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T01:46:30Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for frontend-proxy is explained by 504 responses on the proxy's 'ingress' spans, which are exposed by cart-service failures: cart's own error spans and container logs state exactly 'Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' (ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected). The Redis endpoint served by pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr stopped answering Redis protocol at about 01:46: the in-cluster otel-collector's redis receiver (on a different node) froze its redis_* samples at ~01:46 while its trace/span metrics kept flowing, and cart's Redis client spans (HGET/HMSET/EXPIRE) stopped entirely after the 01:46:30 sample. The valkey-cart pod remained Running/Ready with 0 restarts and a populated Service endpoint, and its measured CPU (0.0014-0.0035 cores vs a 10m limit), working set (3.5-3.9 MiB vs a 10Mi limit), throttling ratio (1.9-6.2%) and container_memory_failcnt (0) do not support resource starvation of the Redis container; cart's own rising CPU-throttling (0.18-0.26 -> 0.62-0.88) and growing memory appear as consequences of the blocked Redis connects and the 15 s proxy timeouts. Why the valkey-cart process stopped responding cannot be determined from the available evidence (no valkey-cart log lines were retrievable, no redis protocol access, change history not integrated), so the conclusion is partial and root_cause is the valkey-cart pod.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's alerting signal is on its 'ingress' server spans: the 10-minute increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy"} at 02:02:00 was 317.93 for span_name="ingress",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR" against 835.27 for the same span with STATUS_CODE_UNSET, while span_name="router frontend egress" had 0 errors; the sampled error spans carry http.status_code 504 with durations of about 15,000,000 microseconds, and the corresponding load-generator client spans also end with 504 at ~15 s.

The frontend-proxy ingress error burst begins between the 01:45:30 and 01:47:30 evaluation points: the 5-minute increase of frontend-proxy ingress ERROR spans was 0 at 01:25:30/01:27:30, 1.11-3.33 per 5 min from 01:29:30 to 01:43:30, 0 at 01:45:30, then 170 at 01:47:30, 393.33 at 01:49:30, 436.67 at 01:51:30, 432.22 at 01:53:30, 435.56 at 01:55:30 and 220.22 at 01:57:30 — an increase of roughly two orders of magnitude over the earlier low background.

The cart service's own error spans give the exact diagnostic: POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem carry status otel.status_code=ERROR with the description 'Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis at cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected() ... ValkeyCartStore.cs:line 97', and their durations are 468,183,414 / 472,782,600 / 476,482,345 / 477,882,272 / 479,682,021 microseconds; the parent frontend spans 'executing api route (pages) /api/cart' and 'GET|POST /api/cart' fail with http.status_code 500 and grpc status 9 FAILED_PRECONDITION carrying the same message.

The running cart container (pod cart-755465879b-t9mf7) repeatedly logged the bare line 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' followed by 'Error status code ...' between 2026-11-17T01:49:43.139 and 01:53:06.242 (the newest 80 of 135 lines matching the filter), with no previous container instance (restart count 0).

cart's Redis client spans stop entirely during the incident: HGET was 1195.56 per 5 min at the 01:46:30 evaluation point (and 1306.67/1248.89 at 01:36:30/01:41:30), HMSET/EXPIRE 567.78/570, and all of them are 0 at the 01:51:30 and 01:56:30 points, while cart's first ERROR series appear only at those later points (POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 14.46 then 19.83, AddItem 16.87 then 26.83 per 5 min).

The Redis backing store is served by pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr (container valkey-cart, image valkey/valkey:8.1.3-alpine, owned by ReplicaSet valkey-cart-58df56c79c): it is phase Running, Ready=True, restarts 0, started 01:13:18; Service 'valkey-cart' exposes port 6379 and its Endpoints list address 100.96.2.228 on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae, the same node that hosts the cart pod endpoint 100.96.2.233 (cart resolves VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379).

A second, independent client of the same Redis endpoint also lost it at about 01:46: the otel-collector's redis receiver (endpoint valkey-cart:6379, collector pod on node i-0a709b85c49d987be) shows redis_cpu_time_seconds_total{state="user"} rising steadily from 2.207822 at 01:40:00 to 2.6249 at 01:46:00 and then remaining exactly 2.6249 through its last sample at 01:54:00, and redis_memory_used_bytes stays 1710360 from the 01:46:30 evaluation point onward after growing from 1436536 at 01:25:30.

The fault localizes to the valkey-cart pod: its Redis endpoint stopped answering at about 01:46 for the cart client on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae (exact 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' errors and a stop of all Redis client spans) and for the otel-collector redis receiver on node i-0a709b85c49d987be (frozen redis_* samples), while the pod itself stayed Running/Ready with 0 restarts and the Service still listed it as a ready endpoint on port 6379.

The valkey-cart container's declared resources are limits cpu 10m / memory 10Mi and requests cpu 2m / memory 4Mi, and its measured usage stays far below them: container CPU usage 0.0014-0.0035 cores, CPU-throttled-period ratio 0.019-0.062, memory working set 3.48-3.88 MiB, and container_memory_failcnt 0 at every evaluation point in the window.

The cart container's CPU throttling and memory grow only after the Redis connects hang: its CPU-throttled-period ratio is 0.1768-0.2581 from 01:24:30 to 01:45:30 and then 0.6191 (01:48:30), 0.8285 (01:51:30), 0.8672 (01:54:30), 0.8840 (01:57:30); CPU usage rises from 0.0089-0.0105 to 0.0258-0.0272 cores and working set from about 57.5 MB to 100.2 MB (limit 165Mi, requests 55Mi, limits cpu 45m).

The whole otel-demo namespace was rolled out at 01:13, before the incident: all 21 pods have status.startTime between 01:13:18Z and 01:15:04Z, ReplicaSet cart-755465879b (owner Deployment cart) and ReplicaSet valkey-cart-58df56c79c (owner Deployment valkey-cart) were created 01:13:18Z with 1/1 ready replicas, and all 21 deployments report 1 ready / 1 available replica.

The previous cart pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s (pod uid 87b4edb6-131e-4521-9f09-81ea23865443) could not be terminated during the incident: 75 Normal 'Killing' events ('Stopping container cart') at 01:49:20Z and 30 Warning 'FailedKillPod' events at 01:49:19Z whose message is 'error killing pod: [failed to "KillContainer" for "cart" with KillContainerError: "rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded", failed to "KillPodSandbox" ... DeadlineExceeded]'; that pod no longer exists and its ReplicaSet cart-9fd895bb7 is gone.

Impact is carried by the cart-calling path and nothing else observed: in the 10-minute error increase at 02:02:00, cart had POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 25.48 and GetCart 18.83, frontend had 'executing api route (pages) /api/cart' 39.88, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 25.48, GetCart 14.40 and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 4.43, checkout had oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 3.32 and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 3.32, and frontend-proxy ingress 317.93, while the returned series for ad (flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean and EventStream), payment (GET, dns.lookup, tcp.connect), accounting (orders receive), recommendation (flagd EventStream) and fraud-detection (flagd ResolveInt/EventStream) were 0.

product-catalog served normally inside the same sampled traces: its oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct server spans return rpc.grpc.status_code 0 in 96-143 microseconds while the cart and proxy spans in the same traces fail, and all 5 cluster nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure False.

Candidate 1 (leading): the valkey-cart process itself stopped serving the Redis protocol at about 01:46 (e.g. internal hang/blocked event loop/connection backlog) while its container kept running; this is the only candidate consistent with both the same-node cart client and the other-node collector losing valkey-cart:6379 at the same time. The mechanism inside valkey is unverified.

Candidate 2 (remaining, weakly supported): the tight valkey-cart resource settings (limits cpu 10m / memory 10Mi, requests cpu 2m / memory 4Mi) starved the Redis process into unresponsiveness. The measurements in the window argue against it (CPU 0.0014-0.0035 cores, throttling 1.9-6.2%, working set 3.48-3.88 MiB, memory failcnt 0), so it stays a configuration risk rather than an evidenced cause.

Candidate 3 (unresolved): the 01:13 replacement of the valkey-cart pod by ReplicaSet valkey-cart-58df56c79c left a configuration or state that degraded later. The rollout precedes the Redis loss of about 01:46 by roughly 33 minutes and no evidence ties the two, so this remains a coincidence in time rather than a demonstrated cause; what changed in the Deployment is unknown because change history is not integrated.

Hypothesis that the valkey-cart container was resource-starved is contradicted by its own cadvisor readings: CPU usage far below the 10m limit, CPU-throttled-period ratio never above 0.071, working set below 4 MiB against a 10Mi limit, and container_memory_failcnt 0 at all points.

Hypothesis that a node-level fault on i-0146cb0d0caf26bae (where both cart and valkey-cart run) caused the outage is not supported: all nodes report Ready with no MemoryPressure, DiskPressure or PIDPressure, and other pods on that node kept working during the burst — frontend-proxy emitted its 504 spans, product-catalog answered GetProduct with rpc.grpc.status_code 0 in 96-143 microseconds, and the cart container itself was running and logging.

Rejected: the fault-injection flag 'cartFailure' ('Fail cart service') in ConfigMap flagd-config, key demo.flagd.json, is the root cause. Its current value is defaultVariant "off", and the observed failure path is a Redis connection failure inside ValkeyCartStore (not an injected cart-service failure), so the declared fault does not match the failure path; the flag's value at 01:46 could not be verified because change history is not available.

Rejected as the alert's cause: the termination problems of the old cart pod (75 Killing / 30 FailedKillPod events with DeadlineExceeded at 01:49:19-01:49:20) happened after the frontend-proxy error burst began at ~01:45:30-01:47:30 and describe removal of a pod that was not in the cart Service endpoints; it is a separate observation about that pod's container being unkillable, not evidence for the origin of the Redis connectivity loss.

Restore cart storage reachability first: check the valkey-cart container directly (valkey-cli PING/INFO from inside the pod, container logs including the previous instance, container runtime state on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae) and restart pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr only after capturing that state, then confirm Redis protocol availability from another node (e.g. the otel-collector redis receiver resuming samples).

Review the valkey-cart Deployment resources (limits cpu 10m / memory 10Mi, requests cpu 2m / memory 4Mi) against the upstream demo defaults and add a Redis-protocol readiness probe plus an alert on redis_* scrape freshness, since the pod's Kubernetes Ready condition stayed True while its Redis endpoint was unreachable.

gaps: The valkey-cart container's logs could not be read: fetch_pod_logs returned zero lines (status no_data) for valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr/valkey-cart in the window, so whether valkey logged an error, blocked, forked or refused connections is unknown — not evidence of absence.

No Redis-protocol evidence after ~01:46: an instant query for redis_memory_used_bytes or redis_cpu_time_seconds_total at 02:02:00 returned nothing, so valkey-cart's current responsiveness and internal state are unknown.

No change history is integrated, so why all 21 otel-demo pods were replaced at 01:13:18-01:15:04 and whether any Deployment/config changed near 01:46 cannot be established; the valkey-cart pod template and image digest history are unknown.
The NetworkPolicy query returned no objects (status no_data), so cluster network policy coverage for otel-demo could not be confirmed either way; no NetworkPolicy-based explanation is claimed.
Kubernetes events for otel-demo are only present from 01:29:18, so no events were available for the 01:13 rollout (no SuccessfulCreate/Scheduled records) or for anything before 01:29.

kube-state-metrics series (kube_replicaset_owner, kube_pod_owner, etc.) returned no data from this Prometheus, so ownership facts come only from the Kubernetes API and ReplicaSet objects; the previous cart/valkey-cart ReplicaSets no longer exist to inspect.

list_prometheus_rules for RequestErrorRate returned no rule, so the alert's exact expression, threshold and evaluation window are unknown; the reported 'current: 1.0889' value could not be reproduced from a rule definition.

The reason the old cart pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s became unkillable (KillContainer/KillPodSandbox DeadlineExceeded) is unknown: its container state, node i-00702f4ac466cf00 container-runtime health and its logs are unavailable now that the pod is gone.

No direct observation of connection state (TCP/SYN, conntrack, kube-proxy) between cart/otel-collector and valkey-cart exists in the available data, so whether the break is inside the valkey process or in the pod network path is unresolved.
next_steps: Capture valkey-cart state before acting: read container logs (including any previous instance), run valkey-cli PING/INFO/LATENCY from inside the pod and from another pod on a different node, and record whether connections are refused or time out.
Escalate to the platform owner the FailedKillPod DeadlineExceeded events for pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s on node i-00702f4ac466cf00 and check containerd/kubelet health on that node.
Ask for change history for Deployments cart and valkey-cart (and the flagd ConfigMap) around 01:13 and 01:46 to determine whether a configuration or image change triggered the Redis loss of service.

Compare valkey-cart's cpu/memory limits with the upstream opentelemetry-demo defaults and adjust the readiness probe to check Redis protocol, since Kubernetes readiness stayed True while Redis was unreachable.

.items[] | select(.involvedObject.namespace=="otel-demo") | {t:(.lastTimestamp // .eventTime), obj:.involvedObject.kind, name:.involvedObject.name, reason:.reason, msg:.message, type:.type, count:.count}

view.series_note: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics:
    dimensions:
    - default: otel-demo
      name: namespace
exporters:
  clickhouse:
    endpoint: http://clickhouse-clickhouse.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local:8123
    logs_table_name: otel_demo_logs
    password: ""
    traces_table_name: otel_demo_traces
    username: default
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch-master.opensearch.svc.cluster.local:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel-logs
    logs_index_time_format: yyyy-MM-dd
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector.opentelemetry-collectors.svc.cluster.local:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    endpoint: http://prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus.prometheus.svc.cluster.local:9090
    tls:
      insecure: true
  prometheus:
    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:8889
extensions:
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  resourcedetection:
    detectors:
    - env
    - system
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  nginx:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: http://image-provider:8081/status
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  postgresql:
    endpoint: postgresql:5432
    metrics:
      postgresql.blks_hit:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.blks_read:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.deadlocks:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_deleted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_fetched:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_inserted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_returned:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_updated:
        enabled: true
    password: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
    tls:
      insecure: true
    username: root
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
    username: valkey
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - debug
      - prometheus
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - nginx
      - otlp
      - postgresql
      - redis
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - pull:
          exporter:
            prometheus:
              host: 0.0.0.0
              port: 8888
